sentences.text: The petitioner in OP(MV). No.146 of 2001 on the file of Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Attingal, is the appellant.

The petitioner who is the Director General of Police filed the above claim under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation for the damage sustained to Eicher bus bearing registration No KL-01M-3573 belong to the Police Department.

2. The case of the petitioner is that on 8.9.1998, at about 7.35 a.m., a bus bearing No.TR-714 belonging to KSRTC, driven by the 2 nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the Eicher bus belonging to the Police Department and caused damaged to it.
In the claim petition, a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- was claimed as damages.
The Tribunal dismissed the claim petition on the ground that the petitioner has failed to prove the quantum of damage.
Aggrieved by the above Award of the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

3. Now the points that arise for consideration are the following:
2025:KER:20590 1.
Whether the Tribunal was justified in dismissing the claim petition?
2. What is the quantum of damages to be awarded, if any, to the petitioner?

4. Heard Smt. S.L. Sylaja, the learned Government Pleader appearing for the petitioner/appellant,
and Sri. Alex Antony Sebastian P.A, the learned Standing Counsel for the 1st respondent/KSRTC.
5.
The Point: In this case, the accident is not disputed.
The fact that in the accident, the Eicher bus belonging to the petitioner was damaged, was also not disputed.
There is also a police case against the 2nd respondent in that respect.

Exhibit A6 is the copy of the charge sheet involved in crime No.297 of 1998 of Venjaramoodu Police Station in respect of the above accident, in which negligence is attributed against the 2nd respondent.
Now, the only question remains is, what is the quantum of damages sustained by the petitioner?

6. The learned counsel for the petitioner relied upon Annexure A1 proforma in respect of department vehicle showing that the Eicher bus bearing No.KL-01M-3573 was purchased by the Police Department on 2025:KER:20590 6.3.1998 and the purchase cost was Rs.6,67,000/-.
Admittedly, the accident occurred on 8.9.1998, six months and 2 days after it was purchased.
7. Annexure A2, quotation for spare parts issued from Grand Motors Sales Corporation dated 14.7.1999 shows the cost of spare parts required for the vehicle as Rs.72,070.78.

Annexure A3 is the The Director General Of Police vs The Managing Director Of Ksrtc on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34975953/
2 letter issued by the Assistant Executive Engineer, Mechanical Sub Division, Thiruvananthapuram to the Battalion Transport Officer, Battalion Transport Office, KAP III, Thiruvananthapuram stating that for repairing the above bus, a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- is to be spent, which is not economical and hence the vehicle can be condemned for a sum of Rs.95,000/-.
8.

sentences.text: The learned Government Pleader submitted that as per Annexure A3, the vehicle was condemned for a sum of Rs.95,000/-.
The learned Standing Counsel for the KSRTC would argue that in this case, there is no evidence to prove the actual amount spent for repairing the vehicle.
9. It is true that in this case, there is no evidence to prove the actual amount spent for repairing the bus as argued by the learned Standing Counsel.
It is because, in this case the vehicle was not actually repaired to make it 2025:KER:20590 roadworthy.

Instead, it was condemned, as the Assistant Executive Engineer, who assessed the damages opined that repairing the bus will not be economical,
and hence he recommended for it's condemnation.
From Annexure A3, it is revealed that at least a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- was to be spent for making the bus roadworthy.
Since it was found that repairing of the vehicle was not economical, the Assistant Executive Engineer, Mechanical Sub Division recommended for condemning the vehicle for Rs.95,000/-.

10. In the above circumstances, from the available evidence, there is every reason to hold that the petitioner is entitled to get at least a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- towards the cost of damage sustained to the vehicle involved in the accident.

In fact, the loss sustained by the petitioner on account of the accident was much more than Rs.2,00,000/-, as from Annexure A1 it is revealed that it was purchased in March 1998 for a sum of Rs.6,67,000/-.
Because of the damage sustained, it could not be used after 6 months and was to be condemned for a paltry sum of Rs.95000/-.

In the above circumstances, considering the fact that the vehicle belonging to the petitioner has to be condemned because of the damage sustained due to the accident, Rs.2,00,000/- now claimed by the petitioner is quite just and reasonable.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to get a compensation of Rs.2,00,000/-
towards the damage sustained to the department vehicle.
11. In the result, this appeal is allowed.

The 1st respondent is directed to pay/deposit a sum of Rs.2,00,000/-, along with interest @ 8% per annum, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
12.
On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.

Sd/-
C. PRATHEEP KUMAR, JUDGE sou.
